key_insight: MotiMotion reframes motion-controlled image-to-video generation as a reasoning-then-generation task: a visual-reasoning stage infers causal and commonsense consequences from sparse or imprecise user trajectories, then a generator synthesizes videos that reflect both intent and inferred secondary effects.
problem_solved: User-provided motion controls are often sparse, imprecise, and causally incomplete, producing unnatural or implausible videos by missing secondary consequences of motion.
method: Two-stage pipeline: a visual-reasoning module expands and completes sparse user trajectories by predicting causal, commonsense-consistent motion effects and secondary interactions.
Generation stage conditions on the reasoned motion plan to synthesize videos that align with user intent while incorporating inferred consequences for more plausible dynamics.
Training with paired video data and causality-aware objectives (e.g., synthetic perturbations, consistency losses, and multimodal supervision) to learn robust reasoning and faithful synthesis.
impact: Improves realism and robustness of motion-controlled video synthesis, making interactive content creation, animation, and simulation more reliable with minimal user input. Reduces manual tuning of trajectories and better captures secondary/causal effects.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing two stages: Visual Reasoning (expand/complete trajectories) → Generation (conditioned video synthesis).
Before/after side-by-side video frames: naive trajectory-following vs. MotiMotion (shows corrected secondary motion and interactions).
Causal-graph / trajectory overlay illustrating inferred secondary consequences (e.g., object interactions, induced motion).
Bar/line chart or ablation table showing improvements in realism metrics and user-preference scores across baselines.
paper_title: MotiMotion: Motion-Controlled Video Generation with Visual Reasoning
paper_authors: Lee Hsin-Ying, Hanwen Jiang, Yiqun Mei, Jing Shi, Ming-Hsuan Yang
